title: TREASURER’S OFFICE CLOSED (ELECTION DAY)
full_story:
Don’t forget to get out and exercise your rights as an American citizen and vote.

The polls opened at 6:00am and remain open until 7:00pm tonight.  If you would like a heads up of what the ballot looks like before you arrive, you can visit Clay County Clerk Amy Britton’s webpage to view the sample ballot.  Keep in mind that for county board, you’ll only vote for your specific district, which is listed on your voter ID card.  You can follow this link at claycounty.illinois.gov/county—clerk/ then choose elections and county wide specimen ballot.

Now that you’re armed with that information, here’s something else you should know today, just in case you planned to pay your property taxes and sort of kill two birds with one stone…be advised that the Clay County Treasurer’s Office is closed on today.  They reopen for their regular business hours on Wednesday, November 4th.

title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and move swiftly through a light agenda.

As Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order, she opened the floor to public comment with Nikki Green of Flora Tourism addressing members to speak about the upcoming Kriskindle Market.  She stated the event will be hosted in downtown Flora on Friday December 11th starting at 4:00pm and ending Saturday December 12th at 9:00pm.  Green said they will set up in Gaslight Square and requests that the City closes the 100 block of South Main St., which will be used for food trucks and other activities.  A motion was made and commissioners quickly approved her request.

Mayor Spicer then asked for approval of the meeting agenda and the consent agenda, and it too was approved unanimously.  The latter included past meeting minutes, the Warrant list for the second half of October, the City of Flora 2027 Holiday Schedule and City Council meeting dates for 2027.

In regular business, the mayor congratulated the Wolves and commented on what a special weekend it was, with not only the football team’s big win but also an enjoyable time spent at the Flora Halloween Parade.  Spicer did make note of news about the downtown grants and the submission to City Administrator Mike Stanford about the scope of the work to be performed.  She also stated that they are still waiting for an update from the USDA about Flora’s sewer grant progress.  As she polled commissioners for their comments, the only person to speak was Commissioner Phil Wiley.  He too spoke of the great community events enjoyed this past weekend including the Flora Wolves victory over Central A & M, which started with the tailgate party and continued until the end of the Halloween parade.  He said the support this community shows to these, and other events is simply unbelievable and thanked everyone involved in their execution and everyone involved.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford called on Lee Beckman with Milano and Grunoh Engineers of Effingham for an update on city grants.  Among his comments, Beckman noted the progress on the lead service line inventory.  He mentioned the Safe Routes to School current round is complete with some minor cleanup and final inspection for project closure.  Concerning Flora’s Sewer Grants, he stated he was told to look for a Christmas present in the not too distant future.

Mike Stanford then turned to two agenda items.  First, he asked commissioners to approve and ordinance that rescinds Title 1, Chapter 5, Section 16 entitled Mayor.  He said that it dates back to 1956 and added that City Attorney Bob Coble and Chief of Police Jeremy Ruger urged the council to rescind the ordinance.  Standford said that section gives the mayor the authority to make arrests and release prisoners from custody.  Attorney Coble stated that it also gave commissioners those same powers.  The actual ordinance also states it included the authority to call the militia.  The council voted unanimously to approve the rescinding of the ordinance in its entirety, since the specifics identified are now handled by the laws of the State of Illinois.  Stanford also asked the council to approve payment to USDI (Utility Safety and Design, Inc.) for repairs made to a six-inch high pressure natural gas line over Racoon Creek on Flora’s west side.  Members approved the payment of $176,461 unanimously, with a comment that Flora was fortunate the problem was discovered and repaired before a major incident could occur.

title: ACE PATROLS RESULTS
full_story:
Illinois State Police Troop 9 has released the results of their October Alcohol Countermeasure Enforcement or ACE patrols.

The patrols were conducted throughout Clay, Effingham, Lawrence, Marion, Wayne, and White Counties.

Troop 9 commander captain Bruce Waggoner announced that officers seized multiple violations aimed at detecting impaired driving and the illegal transportation of alcohol or drugs.

In total, state police issued 26 citations or arrests and logged 141 written warnings during the extra detail.

The enforcement activity included two DUI citations, nine other alcohol or drug offenses, 41 speed violations, 45 registration offenses, and 18 driver’s license offenses.

State police remind motorists that alcohol and drug impairment are factors in more than 47 percent of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  The ace patrols are funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: YOUTH HUNT
full_story:
Danny Hecht is having a free Youth Bird Hunt on Saturday November 7th.  The hunt is for those ages 10 – 16 wanting to experience Quail and Pheasant Hunting.  The location is the Hecht farm at 3362 Riffle Road near Iola, about 20 minutes South of Effingham.  The hunt times are from 9 am to 4 pm.

There will be Clay Pigeons for warm up, practice, and instruction.  There will be fields for first timers, as well as fields for the experienced hunters.

There will be a raffle to win a gun.  To help conservation efforts there will also be memberships for Quail Forever available.

Hunters should be sure to get a regular hunting License or an apprentice hunting license.  A gun safety course would be beneficial for Safety.

Please call the dealership and tell the receptionist that you want to attend the Youth Hunt in the morning or afternoon and how many will be attending.  The Phone number is 217-342-4111 or 217-821-4112 or email [email protected].

title: USDA CROP PROGRESS REPORT
full_story:
Fall harvest season is wrapping up across Illinois with 86% of corn and 91% of soybeans harvested as of Nov. 1, according to USDA.  Winter wheat planting is also on the home stretch with 84% planted statewide to start the month.  With 57% emerged statewide, USDA’s first condition rating of the season pegged Illinois wheat at 11% excellent, 47% good, 34% fair, 5% poor and 3% very poor.

There were 6.1 days suitable for field work during the week ending November 1st.  Statewide, the average temperature was 61.3 degrees, 11.8 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.17 inches, 0.58 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 17% very short, 32% short, 48% adequate, and 3% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 17% very short, 32% short, 49% adequate, and 2% surplus.

Corn harvested reached 86%, compared to the 5-year average of 83%.

Soybeans harvested reached 91%, compared to the 5-year average of 85%.

Winter wheat planted reached 84%, compared to the 5-year average of 81%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 57%, compared to the 5-year average of 54%.  Winter wheat condition is at 3% very poor, 5% poor, 34% fair, 47% good and 11% excellent.

title: STATE FAIR TICKETS ON SALE
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA) is helping shoppers make the holidays a little more memorable with two special sales featuring the lowest prices of the season on Illinois State Fair passes and gift boxes filled with Illinois Product favorites.

Beginning Monday, November 9th, fairgoers can get a head start on summer fun with the Illinois State Fair Holiday Sale.  Whether shopping for the fair enthusiast in your life or planning ahead for your own summer adventures, holiday pricing offers the best opportunity to save on admission and carnival rides at the 2027 Illinois State Fair.  Holiday pricing includes; a Mega Pass for $70; which includes unlimited carnival rides every day of the Illinois State Fair.  Jumbo Pass for $80; Gives all the benefits of a Mega Pass, plus unlimited rides on the Giant Slide.  The 11-Day Adult Admission Bundle for $45, the 11-Day Senior Admission Bundle for $30 and a Blue Ribbon Cookbook for $20 for in-person purchases or $25 shipped.

These are the lowest Mega and Jumbo Pass prices of the season, available through December 31st, at 11:59 pm.

For those looking to give a taste of Illinois this holiday season, IDOA is also offering its popular Illinois Product Gift Boxes, featuring a curated selection of locally made products from Illinois businesses.  Two gift box options will be available; the Illinois Product Favorites Box for $60 or the Illinois Product Holiday Box for $40.  Filled with your favorite Illinois Products, these boxes offer a convenient way to shop local and share a little homegrown holiday cheer with family, friends and coworkers.

“The holidays are a great time to plan ahead for the Fair and support Illinois businesses,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture.  “Whether you’re picking up passes for next summer or gifting some of your favorite Illinois Products, there’s something for everyone.”

For the first time, customers purchasing Mega or Jumbo Passes during the Illinois State Fair Holiday Sale can upload their photo during checkout and have their completed passes mailed directly to their home in January.

Customers who take advantage of this convenient new option can skip the in-person redemption process entirely, provided their uploaded photo meets the Fair’s established photo guidelines.

Prefer not to upload a photo?  No problem. Customers can still purchase their passes during the Holiday Sale and redeem them in person beginning in June.

All customers will receive an email confirmation of their purchase, regardless of which option they select.
